source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Nolan — overall, the BOM is exactly the direction I was hoping for, and I really like it. Before we finalize anything, though, I’d like your input on a few details:

• Motors — could 450 RPM be too low for producing a strong, frothy matcha texture? Would increasing the speed make sense if we can still retain enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality, would a stainless-steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk?

• Spout — I want to keep the solenoid approach. For both texture and the overall visual experience, the pour needs to remain clean, controlled, and seamless: mix → open → pour.

• Splash / mess control — events make this especially important. The design should provide:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– a smooth, controlled spout flow without sputtering
– no dripping while the valve is closed
– effective sealing so liquid cannot leak into the base
– a splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — if possible, the bowls and spout components should either be removable or easy to clean.

Everything else looks great. What are your thoughts on these points, and would you adjust anything before we finalize the BOM?

value_updates.control_assignment: one PWM speed controller per mixing station

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
On the motor question, I agree that more speed is appropriate, so I’ve selected replacements that spin at 1800RPM. The PWM controller will provide continuous adjustment from 0 RPM up to 1800 while preserving enough torque to mix the liquids.

Choosing the whisk is more difficult because few available options satisfy all of our requirements. We need a reasonably large mixing head so the entire bowl mixes consistently. The bowl is approximately 13 inch in diameter, whereas the plastic head currently listed on the BOM measures only about 3.6" diameter. By comparison, the original wire whisk I proposed was roughly 6.25" in diameter. Although that whisk is marketed for a 10qt bowl, I think it could still work well in our smaller bowl. A head resembling those on handheld electric frothers or mixers would probably be ideal, but those products are only available in very small sizes.

Splashing is not something I currently expect to be a problem. If the mixing becomes too rough, the motor speed can be adjusted during operation; should testing reveal splashing, we can also install the simple splash guard you suggested.

Cleaning has been considered as well. The bowl is already designed for very easy removal, and I also intend to make the custom spout removable so it can be cleaned easily.

Overall, we are nearly ready, and I’ll update the motor specification to 1800rpm. For the whisk, perhaps we should test 2 styles before choosing the best performer? It is one of the easiest components to exchange for a different design, and a simple adapter should allow us to attach virtually any whisk to the setup.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The whisk works for me. For the motors, I propose setting the maximum speed at 2600—what do you think?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I’m good with this direction because the additional power and adjustable speed range make sense. The 5200 RPM motors work for me as long as we do not run them at maximum continuously; being able to dial them down for slow mixing or increase them for higher-speed frothing is ideal.

With that higher maximum, however, we need to ensure two things:
• splashing remains under control
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming overly aggressive at higher speeds

If necessary, I’m open to adding a splash guard or adjusting the whisk position and bowl depth so the machine continues to operate cleanly. Overall, I approve this approach.
